16. Wireframe Composition Annotations (WF-ANN-*), Assumptions (WF-ASM-*) & Decisions (WF-DEC-*)

Composition decisions

ID Frames Composition and preserved meaning Sources
WF-DEC-001 All frames Chart stays mounted and visibly central. Left drawing strip and right launch rail persist; top toolbar owns manual ticker, timeframe, candles/line, indicators, replay, arrangement and settings. Right rail is not the expanded panel itself. UIS-PAT-006; E01-load-chart.png; UIS-NAV-001–012
WF-DEC-002 001–008/065/073/074/082–085 Default shell shows watchlist and instrument details on the right. 085 closes that drawer to enlarge the plot. 084 now uses the compact floating capsule over the lower chart, not a reserved dock. Run identity/cursor remains in the chart heading. 088 selects the start candidate; 089 shows playing. Starting another point on an existing traded run preserves the current state until inline rewind/restart review. 073 keeps two charts inside the central work area. Drawing selection uses the left strip; numeric anchors/brush points open in an Objects drawer. UIS-REG-001–004; UIS-ADAPT-002; VIS-DATA-001–006
WF-DEC-003 009–016/066/075 Settings float above the retained chart; category navigation left, scoped fields right, internally scrolling body and persistent reason/cancel/apply footer. 075 covers chart/study settings without unrelated simulation terms; simulation scope stays separately named. E07-settings-ready.png; UIS-REG-005–007; UIS-DISC-002
WF-DEC-004 017–024/067 Layouts, saved runs, recovery and own-backup selection stay in a reserved local-work drawer beside the chart (a bottom dock at zoom). Candidate selection is not activation. The working/retained checkpoint, validation and authority meanings remain scoped to the selected work. UIS-REG-008–010; IF-JRN-004/013/014; UIS-PAT-006
WF-DEC-005 025–032/068/076 Trading opens a right-hand entry/target drawer, with positions/orders/results in an expandable dock below the central plot, collapsed by default in paper-entry frames 025/090. Run/cursor remains above the chart and next to trade terms. Floating replay-bar paper shortcuts and the right ticket share that completed decision. The ticket prepares terms; Sell/Buy on the replay strip submits a new entry. A32 supplies grouping, while Units/Risk %, instruments and accounting follow project rules. Targeted close and pending-order modification keep distinct controls and identities. The dock may collapse without discarding results or chart state. A24-trades-state.png; UIS-REG-011–014; UIR-SAFE-004
WF-DEC-006 033–048/069/070/077 Original-event resolution and data continuity open contextual right drawers. Original event/missing reason and compatible resolution stay together. Operational data status cannot expose later replay prices. Closing the drawer does not clear a block, change retained inputs or start playback. UIS-REG-015–020; IF-JRN-010/012; UIS-PAT-002/005/006
WF-DEC-007 049–056/071/078–080 Confirmation is inline inside a reserved replay/work dock below the chart, naming target/version and the actual destructive operation. It is not an independent window or primary destination. Consequence, reason and independent cancel/confirm remain co-present. Unknown publication exposes reconciliation rather than a repeated confirmation. UIS-REG-021–023; IF-CONF-001–003; VIS-STATE-014
WF-DEC-008 057–064/072/081 Output is a conditional export action/detail within the reserved Results dock or chart output dock, not a floating window or independent primary screen. Image and own-run report retain different inclusion fields; source remains pinned if workspace advances. Backup remains in local work, not in future run-bundle viewer. UIS-REG-024–026; IF-JRN-011; UIS-PAT-006
WF-DEC-009 065–072 At effective desktop zoom, wrapped toolbar and collapsed secondary drawers preserve the chart anchor. A reserved scrollable lower task dock leaves the resized plot above it; settings, Go to and the replay capsule may overlay; task fields/consequences and persistent actions remain accessible within the task surface. No stacked replacement page is introduced. UIS-ADAPT-001–006; UIR-A11Y-003/004
WF-DEC-010 All frames Run bundle viewer is reserved in the right launcher rail as disabled future scope. Existing watchlist, trading, objects/inspection, continuity and local-work launchers remain individually named. No future viewer flow or V1 external run-bundle import is inferred. Direct user direction, 20 October 2026; UIS-PAT-006; existing V1 scope exclusions
WF-DEC-011 All charts; 086/087 Place 1D/5D/1M/3M/6M/YTD/1Y/5Y/All at bottom left, then a calendar icon. Keep display time/timezone at the other end where space permits. Calendar opens the floating Go to window with Date/Custom range tabs; date/time, month navigation and cancel/Go to stay in that window. The user explicitly restores A29 placement through UIS-PAT-009. Date/range is viewport navigation, distinct from replay progression and top timeframe. Custom range From/To contents are designed rather than observed. UIS-PAT-007; E01-load-chart.png; A29-range-selection.png; UIR-TASK-002; IF-JRN-001
WF-DEC-012 All frames Settings, Go to date/range and replay controls may float. Other actions reserve side/bottom space, including symbol selection, work/recovery, confirmations and export. The plot is resized rather than covered. Report output remains contextual to Results; rewind review remains contextual to replay. UIS-PAT-008; latest user direction, 20 October 2026
WF-DEC-013 Active replay frames; 088–092 Use A30 for start selection and trace A31/A32’s compact floating replay bar and right paper-sidebar hierarchy. The bar overlays the lower plot/volume region; no full-width controller dock or extra default results dock is inserted. Enable new entries only at a paused completed writable decision with valid current terms. Accepted waiting and event processing have dedicated states; all outputs stay bounded by the same retained run cursor. UIS-PAT-010; UI-REF-001–003; IF-JRN-005/007–009; FR-20/40/53
WF-DEC-014 Replay/paper frames, especially 090 Correct the literal A31/A32 geometry: a compact floating capsule, full-height A32-order sidebar, no expanded Results dock in the default paper-entry frame. Use source-sized 1870×884 frame 090 for direct comparison; keep 1280×800 baseline variants. Current replay/paper derivatives from MP-SET-001-r1 are stale until this correction is reviewed and propagated. UIS-PAT-011; direct user rejection/correction; UI-REF-002/003
WF-DEC-015 All 92 frames / active-chart toolbar Direct user request: replace the Bid-only selector with adjacent Bid and Ask show/hide toggles. Each independently controls its own candle series; support Bid only, Ask only, both and neither without clearing chart axes, drawings or context. Check marks and pressed state identify visible series. Illustrative default remains Bid on / Ask off. These visibility controls do not change replay cursor, historical execution prices or the separately governed calculation basis. Narrow-toolbar controls remain adjacent; interval sync is compacted to avoid collisions. User correction, 20 October 2026; UIR-INFO-001; existing bid/ask provider qualification

State annotations and compound-row branches

Each annotation applies to the matching WF-GROUP, including its material-state/adaptive/disclosure frames. Exact per-frame structural changes and allowed recovery are also printed outside each SVG product surface and stored in frame-index.json. Additional copy variants below must preserve geometry and scope; a future structural change requires revision before G4 finalization.

ID Frames / scope Required branch treatment Sources
WF-ANN-001 WF-GROUP-001 / UIS-VIEW-001 Current history and replay are explicit modes (001/082 versus 084); replay playback/order controls are docked below the plot and above range presets; the top line only identifies run/mode/cursor. Loading keeps old arrays under old labels; an absent range, no search match, warm-up and actual archive end have different reasons (003/083). End never liquidates positions. Every chart retains bottom range controls; 086/087 open floating date/range navigation above the chart without changing replay time. Invalid or beyond-boundary requests preserve prior valid viewport/selection and show a reason. Stale/offline/qualified closure has scoped evidence/time; no fabricated movement. Evaluating/slow-panel values are unavailable under the common boundary. Drawing preview, locked and hidden states preserve object identity; numerical anchors/brush points are available (074). Unknown save reconciles; known failed save retries retention, never the trade/edit. Read-only denies mutation but preserves inspection. UIS-STATE-001–008; UIR-INFO-001–006/012/013; VIS-STATE-001–015 as applicable
WF-ANN-002 WF-GROUP-002 / UIS-VIEW-002 Calculating versus draft preview is labelled temporary. Missing spec/FX, warm-up and invalid fields have explicit absence/error; no numeric zero substitute. Changed scope makes an old estimate nonactionable. Offline local-valid settings remain usable; required missing metadata blocks only the affected apply. Applied working settings and save-failed/unknown checkpoint are separate outcomes; Cancel draft remains available during invalidity. UIS-STATE-009–016; UIR-INFO-005/007/008/013; VIS-STATE-001–015 as applicable
WF-ANN-003 WF-GROUP-003 / UIS-VIEW-003 Empty layouts/runs state no checkpoint. Copy/validation/saving identifies phase and preserves old generation. Unsaved suffix is excluded from a pinned older backup. Known storage/corrupt-input failure blocks affected resume; invalid own-backup candidate rejects entirely. Unknown publication reconciles whole scope before repeat. Offline local work is distinct from denied writer. Confirmation routes to 007; no timeout takeover. UIS-STATE-017–024; UIR-INFO-005/013–016; VIS-STATE-001–015 as applicable
WF-ANN-004 WF-GROUP-004 / UIS-VIEW-004 Sizing/submitting/evaluation is pending, never fill. Retained WF-027 now names submitting original request I-009, run R-014, completed decision and submitted terms; no new entry/advance until completion, acceptance/fill unconfirmed and saving separate. WF-092 remains the distinct event-evaluation endpoint. For estimate-only pending, identify draft/version and pending estimate with prior valid terms retained; do not infer a submitted request. For submission, retain original intent/terms; for evaluation, name the affected occurrence/instruction. These are compound-branch obligations, not interchangeable pending facts. Accepted waiting, effective pending, triggered, filled and cancelled name different instruction facts; a fill additionally requires recorded time/side/price/whole quantity/fees/USD. Reduced or closed position retains identity and protection outcome. Over-close and changed target reject without replacing old valid order. Known rejection permits correction; stale estimate requires current review; uncertain command reconciles the original intent (031), while unknown save preserves an already known working execution. Offline qualified reads and denied writer remain distinct. UIS-STATE-025–032; UIR-INFO-006–011/013; VIS-STATE-001–015 as applicable
WF-ANN-005 WF-GROUP-005 / UIS-VIEW-005 Evidence pending/partial, invalid/inapplicable, unavailable offline and historical/noncurrent event each show a specific reason. Original event/time/prefix never disappears. Compatible whole-effect application blocks new decisions. Known resolved (037) and outcome unknown (077) have different actions; neither auto-plays. WF-077 explicitly disables Start bar/Play/Step as well as Sell/Buy until original publication is reconciled; the adjacent reason persists. Evidence inspection, Return paused and Reconcile publication remain enabled. Only established whole-effect resolution (037) permits manual progression. New-basis evidence uses restart review (080), never silent revaluation. An old epoch cannot resolve a new block. UIS-STATE-033–040; UIR-INFO-006/008–011/013; VIS-STATE-001–015 as applicable
WF-ANN-006 WF-GROUP-006 / UIS-VIEW-006 Unknown freshness is not proven closure. A proven closure variant must state supporting session evidence; no receipt/weekend alone proves it. Catch-up separates requested span, qualified subset and unresolved remainder, with provisional/completed/final labels and no invented progress percentage. Empty/invalid/conflicting responses preserve old qualified catalog. Offline, rate limits and access-denied conditions expose different qualified reasons. Receipt, display lag, storage failure and unknown catalog publication do not share a success status. Replay-origin variant 048 omits later financial observations; revoked authority cannot publish. UIS-STATE-041–048; UIR-INFO-002/012/015; VIS-STATE-001–015 as applicable
WF-ANN-007 WF-GROUP-007 / UIS-VIEW-007 049 reviews rewind; 078 own-backup replacement; 079 layout deletion; 080 updated-basis restart. Object/run delete, reset and same-basis restart substitute the exact owned target/consequence in the same review structure; never reuse rewind suffix or updated-basis copy. Invalid input cannot be overridden. Changed version must be re-reviewed (051). Preparation allows cancellation only before publication where supported (052); known failed prepublication uses unchanged-state outcome (053), not unknown (054). New surviving generation (055) restores focus to surviving work; no automatic archive promise. UIS-STATE-049–056; UIR-INFO-014/013/016; VIS-STATE-001–015 as applicable
WF-ANN-008 WF-GROUP-008 / UIS-VIEW-008 Report 057 and chart image 081 have distinct inclusion semantics. Empty history/absent image values state why (058); preparation/writing pins source (059); workspace advancement preserves that original snapshot (060). Known failed/incomplete artifact (061), outcome unknown (062) and verified matching complete artifact (063) differ. Unknown verifies before repeat. Local output may work offline with permitted local source; invalid/restricted disclosure (064) blocks generation and preserves source. UIS-STATE-057–064; UIR-INFO-010/016; VIS-STATE-001–015 as applicable

20. Risk-Based UI Verification Model (UIV-*)

These are required observable properties, not claimed implementation results. Evidence IDs specify what must be collected during implementation review; Section 21 distinguishes completed design checks from evidence still required. No implementation-standards.md currently prescribes a project mechanism here. Do not infer a test runner, coverage percentage, image-diff threshold or new timing budget. Every state/adaptive row in Sections 18–19 is in scope, including compound branches documented by WF-ANN-001–008 rather than separate screen files.

Verification ID Category / target Required observable property Prohibited outcome Governing sources / visual reference Expected evidence
UIV-JRN-001 Journey / IF-JRN-001; view 001 Search/adopt basis, navigate all discovered history and inspect actual selected OHLC with explicit provider/side/period/time. Go to and presets move viewport, preserving actual run cursor. 100k resident window becomes total-history cap; requested label applied to old arrays; Go to advances simulation. Risk-% input, required valid SL, fee-inclusive estimate and unavailable/invalid branch are distinct; invalid state disables commitment. Direction, terms, sizing, settings or context edits immediately invalidate prior validation/estimates while retaining raw inputs. New side-incompatible levels remain invalid until corrected; fresh results bind the exact draft/context; neither pending nor invalid permits submission. Missing spec/FX becomes zero; quantity fixture becomes a default; planned risk implies max loss. UIV-JRN-008 Journey / IF-JRN-008; view 004 Submission identifies phase, original request/run/boundary and submitted terms; prior valid records stay readable with a reason for disabled actions. Estimate pending, submission pending (027) and event evaluation (092) stay distinct. New entry, pending-order modification and cancellation use named distinct intents, current terms and next-event eligibility; invalid edit leaves valid prior order intact. Limit/Stop expose required entry level; O-008 modification binds original terms/version and Apply modification independently from new entry. Only explicit activation of the matching validated replay Buy/Sell action submits the exact reviewed draft after validity/authority recheck. Ticket direction selection, opposite activation, typing, reopening and validation completion submit nothing; no queued click. Unresolved submission freezes original direction/terms; a new entry needs deliberate preparation. Accepted or triggered displayed as filled; retry of unknown command creates duplicate; chart-side selection changes executable side rules. UIV-STATE-001 Truthfulness / all 64 rows Loading, empty, unavailable, warm-up, known failure, partial, stale, restricted, conflict and UNCERTAIN carry scoped reasons, usable reads and appropriate next action. Pending submission exposes original identity, terms, retained records and unavailable-action reason inside the product surface. Each compound branch in WF-ANN is exercised. Single generic error, false zero, failure substituted for unknown or erased coherent evidence. UIS-STATE-001–064; VIS-STATE-001–015; FAIL-001–023 UIV-EVID-003; UIV-EVID-007
UIV-STATE-002 Truthfulness / views 002/003/004/005/007 Accepted instruction, whole working execution and durable acknowledgement remain separately labelled by identity/version. Known failed retention (015) uses an error mark and VIS-COLOR-013, names working v13 / failed save v13 / retained v12 and retries retention only. Unknown publication uses a question mark and VIS-COLOR-014, reconciles the original occurrence and blocks further mutation/advance (077), distinct from known-resolved 037. Saved success inferred from fill, rollback inferred from missing acknowledgement, blind repeat of command/replacement. 23. AI UI Implementation Handoff

Authority precedence and staleness

Requirements/domain/architecture retain semantic authority. For UI realization, apply architecture-dossier.md → Part I UIR → Part II IF → Part III UIS → visual-system.md VIS → Part IV approved WF → Part V MP/UIV. A lower-level picture cannot override an upper-level guarantee. MP-SET-001-r9 matches all 113 approved r14 sources. Eleven corrected conditional-entry pairs have renewed G5 approval; 102 unchanged pairs retain exact approval. The revision-29 INT-002 UX contract is propagated; independent review remains OPEN until recheck. If governing UIR/IF/UIS/VIS or approved geometry changes, list affected UI-ART entries as STALE_VISUAL_ARTIFACT under UISYN-GAP, invalidate relevant G4/G5 approval and revise/reapprove before implementation relies on them. Source SVG hashes in mockup-index.json detect geometry-source drift; they do not substitute for semantic change review.

6. Detailed findings

UIADV-INT-002 — Missing-SL variant still disagrees about the retained Limit level

  • Status / severity: OPEN — MEDIUM; scope reduced to MP-MOCK-096 light/dark and dependent evidence. Original opposite-side ambiguity and all eleven renewed readbacks are corrected.
  • Type / area: READINESS GAP; draft continuity, state truthfulness and implementation-review consistency.
  • Evidence: UIR-INFO-007; IF-BR-008a; Section 14 revision 29, “Draft and validation identity” and invalid-input transition; UIV-INT-001; UI-IMPL-006 require the same proposed conditional level through pending/invalid validation. MP-096 light and dark show ticket Direction: Buy · Type: Limit, Entry level 1.08420 and ERROR: required SL missing; estimate unavailable; capsule shows the same R-014/EURUSD/completed 09:42 Buy draft but Type: Limit · level Not set. Both Buy/Sell have aria-disabled="true". The actual render confirms both readbacks coexist. WF-096 uses proposed price placeholders rather than declaring absence. revision-r9.json excludes 096; its exact r8 bytes remain approved. check_mockups.py's new 22-SVG readback coverage likewise excludes it.
  • Finding: A missing SL correctly invalidates sizing/submission, but the capsule incorrectly erases the retained entry-level meaning. Validation status and raw proposed values are separate facts under the approved UX contract.
  • Consequence: An implementation copying this endpoint can make the same shared draft appear populated in the ticket and empty in the capsule when an unrelated required field is invalid. Recovery/context preservation and later conformance review become inconsistent across error variants. Disabled actions contain commitment risk, so no BLOCKING/HIGH severity or actual trade failure is inferred.
  • Minimum correction direction: Reconcile proposed-level readback for 096 in both themes while preserving the missing-SL reason, invalid/superseded estimate, disabled submissions and editable retained inputs. Extend the conditional-readback evidence to this retained invalid branch; distinguish absent required entry level from absent SL. No formula or new UX policy is required.
  • Earliest owner: mockup-prototype-designer, current consolidated ui-screen-designer HIGH_FI_AND_VERIFICATION.
  • Affected canonical sections: Parts V–VI, MP/UI-ART-096, UID-004, UIV-INT-001 evidence and UI-IMPL-006 realization. Existing normative contract is sufficient.
  • Downstream stale if corrected: MP-096 pair, actual dependent product SVG/PNG previews, gallery/index/digests, scoped revision/check/render evidence and independent review evidence. Trace actual output changes before widening scope; eleven corrected pairs and unrelated sources should retain bytes.
  • Human visual reapproval: YES, scoped G5 for changed 096 content. G4 stays valid if WF bytes/semantics remain unchanged. Historical approval records stay immutable.

UIADV-VIS-001 — Generic direction selectors still bypass the side palette

  • Status / severity / type: OPEN — LOW; DESIGN DEFECT; carried forward from revision 4 and confirmed in inspected current artifacts.
  • Evidence: VIS-STATE-016 includes sidebar direction selectors; VIS-COLOR-016/017 and UI-IMPL-014 require Buy #14532D on #DCFCE7, Sell #7F1D1D on #FEE2E2 in both themes. MP-025/068/093–096/107–109/111–113 retain neutral Select Buy/Sell controls with blue selection. MP-090 and capsule submission controls retain side roles. Current maintained palette check still omits Select labels.

Use sentence case, explicit bid/ask and USD/quantity units; avoid long all-capital instructions. Right-align comparable numeric columns and align decimal places through typography/column formatting, without altering stored precision or selecting domain rounding. Signs accompany signed changes; a dash must have an explained absence reason rather than masquerade as zero. No critical identifier, price, remainder or consequence is available only as truncated text. [UIR-INFO-001/003/007–010/014; DEFER-004; UIS-ADAPT-003]

Action/status roles

ID Token Value light / dark Meaning Non-color cue / usage

Status foregrounds use content/raised surfaces rather than untested tinted backgrounds. High-contrast focus treatment must also work beside accent-filled controls. Selected surfaces keep normal text and a visible marker; any tint is supplemental. Destructive commands use explicit verbs, not a red icon alone. No financial direction, entry side or P&L sign uses a status token. [UIR-A11Y-002/004/005; UIS-PAT-001/004; UIR-SAFE-001–005]

Accessibility realization and verification obligations

  • VIS-A11Y-001: Under accepted UIR-A11Y-004/005, normal text at least 4.5:1, large text at least 3:1 and required non-text control/meaningful graphical distinctions at least 3:1 against adjacent colors. Evaluate actual state/background pairs and both themes; decorative grids do not carry essential information. Palette arithmetic is not a conformance certificate.
  • VIS-A11Y-002: Focus remains visible and unobscured through selected/hover/error states and temporary layers; focus is a 2-pixel continuous outline with a 2-pixel surface-colored separation. Preserve target label and selected cue independently. [UIR-A11Y-001/003/004; UIS-PAT-004]
  • VIS-A11Y-003: No color-only financial direction, series, status, selection or uncertainty. Distinguish every state in the state matrix by words and appropriate mark/pattern. Numeric/anchor/point alternatives and explicit units remain available. [UIR-A11Y-002/003/005]
  • VIS-A11Y-004: Allow text enlargement, wrapping and sequential non-chart reflow without fixed-size clipping; both charts and primary actions remain reachable. Check required target/risk/consequence content at enlargement rather than merely checking base type size. [UIS-ADAPT-001–004]
  • VIS-A11Y-005: Reduced motion removes optional transitions and animated processing marks; retain phase text, critical feedback and replay controls. [UIR-A11Y-006; UIS-ADAPT-005]

Upstream blockers and contradictions

No new blocking structure, accessibility or architecture contradiction was identified. Part III is the explicit standalone-structure substitute, not a missing-input blocker. All six visual-direction decisions are accepted; no unresolved material VIS-DEC or new VIS-GAP/VIS-CON remains.

Preserve DEFER-001/002 provider/session/finality evidence, DEFER-003 study/tool/step/output conventions, DEFER-004 monetary conventions, DEFER-005 bounded UX defaults, DEFER-006 timing/retry configuration, DEFER-007 technical realization and ADV-VER-001 persistence race verification. They remain prerequisites for their affected work. This artifact chooses no numerical defaults, staleness thresholds, provider behavior, architecture guarantee or storage technology. If a later conflict appears, route structural semantics to the interface-structure owner, interaction semantics to the interaction-flow owner, accessibility capability scope to the interface-requirements owner, and domain/security/resilience changes to architecture; do not solve them by color or hiding information.

Wireframe/mockup stages own exact region placement, widths/heights, chart split orientation, disclosure geometry, temporary-surface geometry, field ordering within approved semantic groups and concrete screen compositions. They preserve all UIS view responsibilities, reading/focus/context rules, required co-presence and adaptation. This document does not assign screen coordinates or select new capabilities. Detailed icon artwork remains downstream within the approved icon language.

2. Foundation Profile and Candidate Tests (IS-*)

Tests: B = a common choice is necessary before the first relevant implementation can start; R = independent slice choices would create substantial incompatibility or migration; N = capability is needed now by approved scope or foundation. Yes means the test passes. Scoped provider prerequisites are present requirements, not optional future features. Packages for them cannot be selected before evidence identifies the real integration.

Strength is REQUIRED or DEFAULT. All standards in this profile are active: inherited architectural obligations retain their source authority; technology and policy choices have explicit Gate G6 approval. Tool installation and proof of capability remain foundation work.

3. Standards Detail and Enforcement Plan

Commands in this section are required future checks, to be wired by an approved foundation brief. Their specification is active; they are not installed tools, existing scripts or passing results. Application roots currently contain governance documents only.

Inherited constraints: IS-FND-001, IS-DATA-001, IS-STATE-001, IS-SEC-001, IS-VERIFY-001

Core semantic owners must remain independent of FastAPI/Pydantic, sqlite3/PyArrow, provider SDKs and renderer objects. Adapters translate into inward-defined values/contracts. UI cannot calculate authoritative fills, fees, coverage or saved success. Background computation produces candidates, while authorized version/epoch checks control publication. A process pool, if measured work requires one, receives bounded immutable inputs and cannot publish authoritative state directly. This is task execution within the local application, not thirteen services or a distributed queue.

Full-history navigation is independent of resident arrays. Preserve nanosecond bars and millisecond ticks with their actual unit and occurrence ordering; never import the older blueprint's millisecond-only rule. Current-history improvement cannot mutate retained run inputs. Working accepted/executed and exact saved versions remain independent.

Enforcement: pytest architecture checks for prohibited imports/capabilities and ARCHV-001–007; deterministic workflow barriers for CONC/IDEM/RETRY/ORDER; real-process reopen/failure tests for TX-003–006 and TF-006. Include ADV-VER-001: catalog publication racing with autosave or scoped run replacement must preserve unrelated acknowledged durable state. UI checks map to actual UIV identities. Static checks and mock storage cannot establish physical durability.

Runtime and transport: IS-FND-002, IS-RUN-001, IS-COM-001

Bind the service to loopback, serve the built client from that origin, and keep one mutation authority per work store. Validate Host and Origin against the launch configuration; reject cross-origin mutations and WebSocket connections. A short-lived, purpose-bound application capability is required in addition to loopback. Do not place it in URLs, logs, backups or persistent browser storage; provider credentials never enter the client. The transport bootstrap must prove that a foreign web page cannot obtain the capability. Development proxying must preserve the same rules rather than enable wildcard CORS.

Use one Uvicorn authoritative worker, exclusive store ownership across processes, per-run ordering and version/owner/run/restore epoch fencing through publication. A second browser tab receives read-only/denied mutation authority. Losing a connection or observing a timeout cannot grant another writer permission while the previous writer can still publish. Acquisition follows application runtime authority and stops/fences callbacks on shutdown or revocation.

FastAPI/Pydantic represent transport validation, not business validity. Export OpenAPI from the service contract and use openapi-typescript for generated TS types. Include update envelope models in the canonical transport schema; enforce schema compatibility for WebSocket messages as well as HTTP responses. Native fetch/WebSocket are sufficient; do not add an additional client state/cache package at bootstrap. Generated declarations do not provide runtime validation: service responses and received messages require controlled decoding/contract checks at the boundary.

Enforcement: HTTP/WebSocket allowed-owner and foreign-origin tests, a two-service exclusion test against the same actual store, stale-epoch publication tests, and schema regeneration with a clean byte comparison. Command retry preserves logical occurrence identity and canonical payload; reconnect refreshes authorized snapshots rather than replaying unsaved intents. No endpoint inventory or new domain command is designed here.

Presentation: IS-UI-001 and IS-UI-002

Use TradingView Lightweight Charts, the browser-side lightweight-charts npm package, as the required chart engine behind the BND-012 renderer adapter. Target the documented 5.2.x API line and freeze an exact compatible released package version during foundation bootstrap. Bundle its JavaScript and dependencies locally with the frontend. Use its native TypeScript API directly; no React wrapper package or vendor fork is selected. The surrounding React choice is approved under G6-DEC-003. Create/dispose chart instances and subscriptions with the UI lifecycle; resize and update existing instances rather than recreating them on each render.

Use semantic DOM controls, task surfaces and readouts around the chart. Keep library objects, chart buffers, viewport transforms and callbacks inside the adapter; core contracts and saved drawings carry semantic values, not IChartApi/series handles or pixels. Shell-local state uses the approved React hooks/reducers/context; canonical run, calculation, catalog and durability state remains service-owned. Explicit context generations prevent adopting obsolete views. Chart callbacks cannot advance replay or execute an instruction. Do not add another global state library until measured complexity establishes present need.

The renderer must support filled Bid / hollow Ask, adjacent Bid-left and Ask-right slots in one true UTC bucket, separate OHLCV and provider-volume readouts, exact active-theme colors, financial drawing anchors, panes, selection and local image export. Never shift actual timestamps to separate candle slots. Geometry can use bounded relative numeric coordinates while original instants/prices remain lossless outside the drawing transform. Virtualize/cull visible geometry; never turn view culling into a history-retention cap.

Customization: Use built-in series/panes where they satisfy the approved design, with adapter-owned custom series for paired candle/volume geometry and primitives for financially anchored drawings or annotations where needed. Two ordinary candlestick series sharing timestamps must not be assumed to provide adjacent side slots. A custom series can carry both quotes for one real UTC bucket and draw separate Bid/Ask slots within that bucket. Prove autoscale, hit testing, crosshair/selection and missing-side readouts against the original bucket identity; use equivalent custom geometry for paired filled/hollow volume bars. Hollow Ask bodies and open/close ticks remain required. Map VIS roles into library options and custom drawing code; library defaults never replace approved tokens. These are implementation requirements to demonstrate, not claims that the library's defaults already meet them. The documented custom-series extension, series primitives and panes provide the intended extension mechanisms.

Data and accessibility: The chart receives already bounded application data; studies, replay, execution, storage and market acquisition remain with their existing owners. Explicitly convert source bar bucket instants to the library's UTC-seconds presentation representation and retain lossless original identities/units separately. Do not pass nanoseconds as JS numbers, collapse distinct events, shift timestamps for quote spacing or feed post-cursor facts to chart autoscaling/legends. Readouts and numeric drawing editing use original values; library canvas interactions do not establish keyboard or screen-reader support. Image export must include the intended chart/custom layers and approved source/boundary labels; verify any separately overlaid DOM/SVG content rather than assuming the library screenshot includes it.

Distribution and attribution: Follow the selected release's Apache-2.0 LICENSE/NOTICE and documented creator attribution/link instructions. Include its notices in local distribution and make the notice plus TradingView link available in application-accessible attribution content. A plain-text library credit can preserve VIS-CONT-003's local application identity; selecting this library does not authorize TradingView product branding or account/upgrade decorations. The optional on-chart attribution logo is not required by this spec; if selected later, route its placement through the UI owner. Runtime assets remain local and no background TradingView data request is introduced. Attribution guidance is recorded from the official getting-started documentation; confirm against the exact installed release at packaging.

Rationale/trade-off: This is the user's explicit chart-engine choice. It reuses chart scales, panes and navigation while retaining adapter-owned custom quote geometry, drawings, accessible controls and export composition. No claim that the library alone meets P3 or supplies these complete application features is made. Replacing the engine or maintaining a vendor fork requires an explicit standards revision; a slice cannot silently substitute the earlier standalone Canvas engine.

Enforcement: frontend unit/component tests for transforms and truthful state; Playwright for keyboard/numeric alternatives, original coordinates, visual comparison and UIV-DATA-003/VIS-002; TF-010 on recorded hardware with two charts, 100k resident bars/chart, four study panes and 100 drawings. Ready-local initial viewport <2s, interaction p95 <50ms, display within 1s of local receipt remain the accepted targets. If this realization cannot meet them, return its technology decision for revision rather than weaken the targets.

Persistence and exact representation: IS-STORE-001 and IS-NUM-001

SQLite is the durable metadata/reference publication mechanism; app-owned immutable files retain selected evidence and acquired history. PyArrow reads the actual Parquet schema in the external-source adapter and writes owned Parquet without silently coercing precision or occurrence identity. No ORM or general analytical SQL engine is needed at bootstrap. SQL migrations are numbered, ordered and tracked; test empty creation and supported-version upgrades before activation. Physical schemas are future implementation work under the existing conceptual ownership.

Stage, verify and durably retain complete referenced file content before atomically committing its active metadata reference. SQLite and filesystem writes are not a shared transaction: never reference incomplete files, acknowledge before durable closure, or let cleanup reclaim pinned content. Keep work/catalog publication compatible with unrelated committed state. Choose database settings and file flush/directory publication procedures in the foundation brief, then prove them with actual crash/reopen frontiers and negative tests. Merely selecting SQLite does not discharge TX-004/TX-005 or DEFER-007.

Keep the active store on a tested local filesystem outside this Google Drive checkout; configure its location explicitly. Do not assume synced/network filesystem locking or durability. Source read roots and owned write roots are separate. This choice does not supply the missing architecture-owned Data location adoption contract. Backups of owned work remain included; contract-v1.0.0 external-run import remains excluded.

Represent original instants as integers with explicit units internally and decimal integer strings over JSON where required to avoid JS precision loss. Use Decimal constructed from exact source representations for monetary calculations; do not use the process default context as an undocumented policy. Reject non-finite inputs. BND-009 must supply approved precision, rounding, quantity steps and independent examples under DEFER-004 before monetary behavior is implemented. This technology choice selects no financial rounding rule or inferred instrument value. Renderer floats must never round-trip into retained values implicitly.

Enforcement: pytest persistence/round-trip/migration tests for TF-006/007, ARCHV-003/006 and AUDV; interruption before/after content retention and reference commit, lost acknowledgement, source mutation, full disk, two-process ownership, stale saves, backup pinning and concurrent catalog/work publications. Compare original precision and whole recovered state; validate rejected candidates leave prior state intact.

Dependencies, packaging and verification: IS-PKG-001, IS-BUILD-001, IS-QA-001

Use CPython 3.14.x and Node 24.x; Node is build/test tooling, not a second application service. uv manages the backend project and frozen lock; npm manages one frontend package and lock. Keep authoring-tool dependency groups separate from product runtime. For the existing contract tools, use their own environment/lock if they are maintained; do not add PyArrow to the standard-library-only evidence extractors.

Record exact interpreter, Node, tool and dependency versions in foundation evidence. React 19.x / TypeScript 6.x / Vite 8.x are approved compatibility lines; Lightweight Charts targets the documented 5.2.x line under the user-selected engine decision. Resolve and commit exact compatible released package pins during foundation bootstrap with clean install/build evidence. No floating latest resolution in verification or distribution. Major-line or capability changes require standards reconsideration. Official support documentation is research evidence, not proof that this repository's dependency set has been installed together.

Release locally built assets with the locked Python application. Runtime must work with local retained history and all UI assets offline; provider recovery separately requires network access. Provide a single documented local launch/stop path and actual readiness checks through the foundation brief. An installer, container or desktop wrapper is unnecessary for this baseline. Preserve the separate offline dossier build/package workflow.

Required backend checks after bootstrap: uv sync --frozen, uv run ruff check ., uv run ruff format --check ., uv run basedpyright, uv run pytest. Run within backend/ once configured. Use Ruff E4/E7/E9/F/I/B/UP rules without formatter-conflicting layout checks, 88-column formatting and basedpyright strict for new backend code. Required narrow suppressions name a reason; no broad whole-project disabling.

Required frontend checks after bootstrap, within frontend/: npm ci, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm run test -- --run, npm run build, npm run test:e2e. Foundation must define these scripts. Use tsc --noEmit with strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes; ESLint with typescript-eslint and React hooks rules; Prettier for formatting; Vitest/Testing Library for local behavior and Playwright Chromium for browser journeys. Record actual browser versions; other desktop engines may be checked for compatibility but are not silently certified. No additional production OS/installer support claim is selected by using Chromium for automation.

ARCHV import/effect checks belong to pytest and the scope's lint rules, with allowed dependencies traced to DEP-*; forbid framework/storage/vendor imports inward and provider/latest calls from replay panels. A syntactic parameter check cannot prove historical boundedness. UIA11Y checks require keyboard/focus/reflow observation, beyond lint or static SVGs. Test only relevant properties per brief; no duplicate arithmetic E2E suite, blanket coverage target, arbitrary test sleeps or network-required default tests. Controlled fixtures never certify provider/session/finality access.

Configuration and diagnostics: IS-OPS-001

Service configuration declares confined read and owned storage/export roots, runtime limits and provider-independent settings. Reject invalid configuration before acquisition or mutation; do not guess a valid source root from a manifest. Keep secret material in service-only launch configuration supplied by the user/integration environment; do not prescribe a credential-entry UI or provider SDK before DEFER-001. Do not publish secrets via frontend environment variables, errors or generated schemas.

Use stdlib logging with structured JSONL rotation and monotonic phase timings. Opaque operation/generation identities may correlate LOG/TRACE records, never metric dimensions. Exclude raw provider payloads, credentials/capabilities, private captured identities, arrays and complete financial histories. Persist semantic AUD facts with owning state, independently of diagnostic retention. Local status UI consumes explicit normalized outcomes rather than log messages.

Approved initial diagnostic budget: maximum 10 MiB current log plus four rotated files, oldest first; bounded diagnostic events at most 16 KiB each. Truncate/drop oversized diagnostic fields with an explicit marker; never truncate semantic retained evidence. This is a tunable engineering resource budget, not a provider deadline or retention limit on market/run data. Publish dropped-event/rotation counts locally. Before any timed scheduler/provider behavior, its brief must supply finite validated bounds, cancellation, provider-feedback handling and performance evidence under DEFER-006. Staleness/session thresholds remain unresolved; no receipt means unknown freshness rather than closure.

Enforcement: configuration rejection, secret-sentinel exclusion, log-rotation/size tests, bounded metric labels, and measurement linking MET-001–005/TRACE-001–004 to DIAG-001–009. No remote telemetry or market-alert subsystem is introduced.

Python operational profile (active scoped guides)

Use four-space indentation, snake_case functions/modules/variables, PascalCase classes and UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constants. Group standard-library, third-party and local imports; avoid wildcard imports. Use pathlib for controlled paths. Comments/docstrings explain contracts and reasons. New backend interfaces are typed, with unknown data validated at adapters; keep framework models outside core. Expected invalid/prerequisite outcomes are explicit results, unexpected errors retain safe causal context, and transport errors are sanitized. Tests name the protected observable rule and use independent expected results, temporary owned paths and deterministic barriers.

Project clarification: Ruff formatting at 88 columns replaces PEP 8's usual line target for new backend code. Existing authoring scopes retain surrounding quote/layout conventions in untouched regions; formatter adoption must not regenerate approved visual bytes incidentally. Original root AGENTS.md deterministic/offline/standard-library rules remain applicable to the dossier tools; FastAPI/PyArrow exceptions belong to their approved application adapters, not extractors. These scoped distinctions and the stated formatting/JSX/SQLite adaptations were approved under G6-DEC-009.

TypeScript/TSX operational profile

Use ES modules, named exports, camelCase values/functions and PascalCase types/components; use type-only imports where appropriate. Prefer unknown to any at untrusted boundaries and narrow before use. Avoid non-null assertions and broad lint suppression; represent material outcome variants explicitly. Keep semantic identities/units distinct from display strings and mutable renderer handles. Hooks follow React's rules; effects subscribe/clean up against their context rather than duplicate canonical state. Test behavior through accessible controls; inject async completion to exercise stale results.

Project adaptations: Prettier controls mechanical formatting; React function components/JSX and CSS Modules are permitted. Generated transport declarations are excluded from manual style edits and regenerated from the canonical schema. Native browser number/date conversion cannot authorize financial rounding or truncate original timestamp precision.

HTML/CSS and SQL operational profile

HTML uses semantic elements, explicit labels, valid nesting, explicit closing tags and safe text insertion. CSS uses two-space formatting, scoped classes and semantic custom properties; root token definitions are the only approved visual-literal registry. No inline captured markup or output-directory style edits. These rules adapt the primary Google HTML/CSS profile to JSX, locally served assets and canonical VIS roles.

SQL uses SQLite-supported syntax, uppercase keywords, snake_case identifiers, explicit columns and bound values. Migrations are immutable after accepted use; a subsequent migration evolves persisted representation. Test supported upgrade paths and failure preservation. Domain invariants, concurrency and filesystem durability are not inferred from DDL success. This is a project-authored SQLite profile, not a claim of an official SQLite formatting standard.

Authenticated TradingView inspection — 16 October 2026

The logged-in session allowed direct verification of workflows that stopped at registration in the original investigation. Drawings, RSI, save/reload, two-chart interval synchronization, historical replay, Pine compilation, and strategy reports now have working reference evidence. Alert configuration and paper-trading interfaces were inspected; alert delivery and order execution were not exercised.

This update supplements the original analysis and changes its coverage conclusions. The local implementation guide incorporates the resulting behavioral requirements. The proposed local application is still an independent reconstruction; this investigation did not recover TradingView's source or build the application.

Session, method, and evidence boundaries

REA discovered the user's existing authenticated chart tab. A second tab in the same browser shared its authentication. The generic SPX chart link initially resolved to an existing saved workspace, so a separate layout named Codex inspection 2026-10-16 was created before chart mutations. The original tab was not used for those mutations. This also demonstrates that a generic chart URL and requested symbol do not alone specify the authenticated initial workspace. [A01–A03]

The update retains 35 controlled scenarios, 290 steps, and 27 selected screenshots: 244 steps completed, 10 failed, and 36 were cancelled. These counts include scenario-start navigation and measure inspection activity, not application coverage. Failed locators, intercepted clicks, and later recoveries are retained. The authenticated index maps A01–A35 to full REA Evidence IDs, declared actions, artifacts, outcomes, and limitations. E01–E18 remain the separate 15 October anonymous baseline.

The browser was an externally owned CDP target, not an isolated profile. REA reported Chromium version 8.2.4133.87; CDP's product string was Chrome/8.2.4133.87. These are reported identities, not an independently verified engine build. A supplementary DOM read measured 1879 × 916, DPR 1, despite the earlier scenarios requesting 1440 × 1000. Do not use the requested viewport as measured geometry. Early scenarios requested Asia/Bangkok emulation; later scenarios used the provider's UTC default. The chart displayed UTC+7. Browser emulation, chart display timezone, and instrument exchange timezone are separate settings.

The packaged review derivative masks account names, existing layout identifiers, private script IDs, and account summary figures in text. Original Evidence IDs identify source records; each modified text artifact has a derivative digest and its original digest. Selected screenshots retain original pixels and ordinary signed-in UI. Screenshots of private account balances and EURUSD ticket margin values are excluded. The complete authenticated export remains outside the distributable package. No cookies, storage values, request/response bodies, header values, or authenticated WebSocket payloads were collected.

RSI, indicator panes, and persistence

The indicator directory contains duplicate DOM identities for the favorite and technical-result entries of STD;RSI. Choosing the first matched built-in entry successfully added RSI. A pointer click on its settings control was intercepted by the canvas; keyboard activation of the same control opened the dialog. These failures reflect locator/interaction paths, not evidence that settings are unavailable. [A04–A07]

For the captured SPX daily state, the data window displayed close 7744.06, RSI 51.94, and RSI-based MA 55.09. These are observation fixtures, not a proof of formula equivalence. A replacement must match the same provider history, corporate/session rules, initialization, warm-up, bar finality, and rounding before comparing outputs. [A05, A07–A08]

The inspected RSI settings were:

Tab Captured settings
Inputs Length 14; source Close; Calculate Divergence unchecked; smoothing SMA, length 14; BB StdDev 2 disabled; calculation timeframe Chart; Wait for timeframe closes checked
Style RSI and RSI-based MA plots; upper/middle/lower bands 70/50/30; background and overbought/oversold fills; precision Default; price-scale/status-line display options
Visibility Ticks; seconds 1–59; minutes 1–59; hours 1–24; days 1–366; weeks 1–52; months 1–12; ranges

The dialog was cancelled without changing these settings. Saving with Control+S and reloading restored the RSI pane, establishing persistence across a real page reload rather than merely keeping an in-memory component alive. Separate data, presentation, visibility, and timeframe policies are therefore useful in the local indicator schema. [A07–A08]

RSI Inputs screenshot · Style · Visibility

Drawings and command history

Selecting Horizontal line and clicking the plot created a line near 7099.39. Control+Z removed it, Control+Y restored it, and the Object tree listed the line beside the chart and indicators. A later reload retained the drawing. Double-clicking it opened settings; the Coordinates input was edited to 7100.00, applied, and saved. Style included a price-label option. [A08–A09]

The local drawing record needs a price anchor with instrument identity and display precision. Screen coordinates are an input/rendering concern. Commands should record creation and coordinate edits, allowing undo/redo without duplicating objects. Serialization must preserve the drawing across reload independently of renderer object identity. These observations cover one horizontal line, not the full tool catalog.

Drawing coordinates screenshot · Object tree

Multi-chart layouts and synchronization

A two-column layout successfully instantiated two SPX chart regions with studies. The underlying interval-sync switch reported aria-disabled=true and refused direct pointer activation, including through its label. Keyboard Enter on its containing row toggled selection; selecting one hour then changed both headers from 1D to 1h. A save and reload restored two charts. The layout was subsequently returned to one daily chart and saved. [A17–A20]

The original E04 one-chart disabled-switch observation must not be generalized into an account restriction. In the authenticated state, the row was usable through a different interaction path. A local implementation should provide consistent pointer and keyboard behavior and store interval synchronization as explicit layout state. Synchronizing symbols, crosshairs, clicked times, or visible ranges remains unverified.

Synchronized chart screenshot · Restored two-chart layout

Historical replay

Bar replay exposed a historical start selector, play/forward controls, speed, and Replay Trading. Selecting a historical point changed the chart and indicator values; stepping forward changed OHLC and RSI again. In the captured step, RSI changed from 66.57 to 61.45 and its moving average from 71.73 to 71.37. The data-window date remained a hover date, so it cannot establish the next replay timestamp. Last-day change continued to show live information. [A13–A14]

The speed menu listed 10x, 7x, 5x, 3x, 1x, 0.5x, 0.3x, 0.2x, and 0.1x, with labels from ten updates per second down to one every ten seconds. These labels were inspected; actual cadence was not benchmarked. Exiting opened Leave current replay?, an unchecked Save this replay option, and Leave/Stay choices. Leaving without saving returned the chart to current data. [A14–A16]

A local replay clock must bound bars and studies independently of the live quote stream. Crosshair date, replay cursor, last visible bar, and latest live quote must remain distinct. Otherwise a UI can look correct while simulations read future observations. Saved replay and replay order execution need further reference tests.

Historical replay screenshot · Forward step · Speed options

Alert creation forms

Creating an alert while the horizontal line was selected preselected Price / Crossing / Horizontal line and showed a once-per-bar trigger. Opening an ordinary price alert showed SPX / Price / Crossing / numeric value, an additional-condition action, expiration, Message, and Notifications. The condition list exposed Crossing, Crossing Up, Crossing Down, and Show more. The ordinary price trigger menu distinguished Once only from Every time; its description says Every time triggers once per minute while the condition remains met. These semantics are specific to this captured condition context. [A09–A11]

Message opens an alert-name field, message editor, placeholder insertion, and Apply/Cancel. Notifications offered app, toast, email, webhook URL, sound and repetition, alternate plain-text email, and a notification schedule with muting outside that schedule. In the captured state app/toast were checked, email/webhook were unchecked, the URL input was disabled while webhook was off, and sound was 3 Notes Reverb once. No address or webhook was entered. [A11–A12]

No alert was created. The local design needs condition-dependent evaluation and frequency, expiration, templated messages, channel preferences, and a persistent scheduler if alerts run with the browser closed. Form presence supplies no evidence of delivery reliability, webhook protocol, server retry behavior, or quota semantics.

Price alert screenshot · Trigger menu · Notifications

Pine compilation and strategy reports

Only newly authored probe scripts were used. The untouched starter editor was replaced with this Pine v6 indicator:

//@version=6
indicator("Codex inspection SMA", overlay=true)
plot(ta.sma(close, 20), title="SMA20")

Add to chart compiled it and displayed SMA20 on the price chart and in the data window, with 7738.79 for the captured SPX state. This verifies an executing script path. It does not establish a local equivalent SMA result without a matching dataset. [A20–A21]

An initial crossover-strategy typing probe hit CE10188 because the editor's autoindent placed the entered plot in local scope. This was an input construction issue; the UI correctly exposed a diagnostic and a no-trades state. A global-only mechanics probe then compiled successfully:

//@version=6
strategy("Codex inspection strategy", overlay=true, initial_capital=100000)
strategy.entry("L", strategy.long, qty=1)
strategy.close("L")
plot(ta.sma(close, 20), title="SMA20")

This deliberately simple script exercises report generation, not a meaningful trading strategy. The captured report showed total PnL, drawdown, trade count, profitable-trade fraction, profit factor, equity visualization, and performance-analysis areas. The displayed SPX report currency was NONE, so its numerical results must not be relabeled USD. Its displayed historical range was not independently validated. List of trades exposed entry/exit timestamps, prices, size, net PnL, return, Show on chart, column setup, and Download .csv. Download was not clicked. [A22–A24]

Strategy Properties exposed initial capital 100000, currency Same as chart, default size 100% equity, pyramiding 1, Default bar detalization (4 ticks/bar), On bar close execution, commission 0 Percent, 1x long/short leverage, slippage 0 ticks, limit orders at Requested price, and One tick order delay. The probe's explicit qty=1 overrides its default order-size setting. The dialog was cancelled without changes. These settings are part of a reproducible backtest contract; an equity plot alone is insufficient. [A24]

Strategy report screenshot · Trades · Execution properties

The Pine network summary records remote pine-facade.tradingview.com calls during these probes, including POST /pine-facade/save/new_draft, POST /pine-facade/translate_light, and permission/translation requests for private USER script identities, which are masked. No bodies or credential/header values were captured. The timing associates remote compilation and draft persistence with Add to chart; it does not recover compiler internals or establish where every study calculation executes. Compilation created remote draft state even without an explicit named Save or Publish. A local editor therefore needs its own supported interpreter/compiler or an explicit bounded script model.

Paper simulation and order-entry surfaces

The broker chooser allowed connection to Paper Trading. No real broker connection or order submission was performed. An SPX order ticket stated Indices can't be traded directly, directing users toward derivatives. This confirms the capability warning anticipated from E01 metadata; visible Buy/Sell boxes do not establish tradability. [A25–A28]

Changing only the inspection chart to OANDA:EURUSD exposed a usable ticket: Buy/Sell quotes, Market/Limit/Stop modes, Units quantity, margin/leverage and pip-value information, take-profit/stop-loss exits, and order review/submit controls. Limit and Stop added price and time-in-force, with Week visible in this state. None of the submit actions were used. Market and Order mode were restored after inspection. [A29–A32]

DOM mode showed a price ladder with bid/ask levels and Flatten, CXL All, Reverse, Buy Mkt, and Sell Mkt actions. These were inventoried without activation. The account manager exposed Positions, Orders, Order history, Balance history, Activity log, Trade history, and Analytics, plus a position grid with prices, quantities, exits, PnL, leverage, margin, and expiration columns. Positions was empty. Other account tabs were not traversed. Existing simulator account figures were excluded from the review text and screenshots. [A31–A32]

The local implementation should separate a disposable order draft from a submitted order and keep replay simulation distinct from live paper trading. Contract size, tick size, quantity units, quote currency, margin, and supported order types belong to instrument/broker capabilities. Fill rules, partial fills, rejection, cancellation, amendments, accounting parity, and recovery remain open.

Cleanup and outstanding verification

The inspection created a separate saved layout and remote Pine draft state. Alerts were cancelled rather than created; no orders or publications were submitted. The original chart tab was not selected for chart mutations. Multi-chart testing ended by saving the inspection layout as one daily chart; later Pine and symbol probes may have been autosaved by the application. Treat this inspection layout as disposable.

REA releases its CDP connection as disconnected-external and does not own the browser process. Several simulator-disconnection attempts failed because of transient menu state and selectors. Supplementary native browser interaction opened the Paper Trading context menu and invoked its broker Log out item; a later snapshot no longer showed the account manager. This was broker logout, not TradingView account logout. The browser endpoint temporarily became unavailable during tab cleanup. After reconnecting, the original EURUSD tab was verified still present and restored to the foreground, and the inspection tab was closed successfully. Final broker status was not independently confirmed by reopening its connection UI. The scratch layout/draft were not deleted. [A32–A35; supplementary cleanup notes]

The largest remaining parity obligations are full Pine compatibility, formula/history equivalence, all drawing tools, alert delivery and persistence, actual order lifecycle/accounting, saved replay, layout conflicts, watchlist editing, advanced chart types, and intermediate responsive/touch behavior. The original startup network capture remains bounded to E01. No original server/source implementation was recovered.

Regenerate the packaged authenticated extracts offline with:

python analysis/tradingview/extract_authenticated_evidence.py
python analysis/tradingview/build_viewer.py

The extractor validates derivative text and selected-image SHA-256 digests. It never executes captured page content. See README.txt for package structure and LOCAL-IMPLEMENTATION.md for the architecture and expanded acceptance criteria.

TradingView Supercharts local replication analysis

The inspected application is TradingView Supercharts at https://www.tradingview.com/chart/?symbol=SP%3ASPX. A useful local equivalent can reproduce its chart workspace, instrument search, watchlists, indicators, drawings, layouts, replay, and paper simulation. The strongest starting point for a personal localhost application is Lightweight Charts with a custom TypeScript application and local data service. The large implementation work is the surrounding behavior, financial data semantics, and persistence.

This package contains live interface evidence and a proposed reconstruction specification. It does not recover TradingView's original source or establish complete behavioral equivalence. Updated 16 October 2026: the authenticated findings establish working drawings, RSI, save/reload, synchronized layouts, replay, Pine compilation, and strategy reports. Alert forms and paper order-entry surfaces were inspected without creating alerts or submitting orders. Numerical parity, full Pine compatibility, order execution, and advanced interactions remain open.

Read LOCAL-IMPLEMENTATION.md for the proposed architecture, data contracts, indicator mathematics, simulation rules, storage, and release criteria. Open index.html for a navigable report and screenshot gallery. The evidence index maps every short reference such as E01 to its full REA Evidence ID, declared actions, outcomes, and extracted artifacts.

Inspection scope and evidence

The original baseline used REA controlled browser scenarios on 15 October 2026, with Chromium 153.0.8010.12, isolated temporary profiles, no account, locale en-US, and device scale factor 1. Desktop captures used 1440 × 1000; the narrow viewport used 390 × 844. The first scenario used America/New_York browser timezone; subsequent scenarios used UTC. These are test-environment settings, distinct from the instrument's exchange timezone. REA reported terminating all browsers it owned. The 16 October authenticated investigation instead attached to an external browser and created a separate inspection layout. Its environment, 35 scenarios, 290 steps, 27 additional screenshots, limitations, and A-series evidence are documented in AUTHENTICATED-FINDINGS.md.

There are 18 retained scenario records, 160 recorded steps, and 32 selected screenshots. Of the steps, 133 completed, 7 failed, and 20 were cancelled after a failure; scenario-start navigation is included in these counts. Failed locators and intercepted clicks are retained, and are not treated as successful feature tests. Later focused captures resolved several locator problems and established registration gates. These counts measure inspection activity, not product test coverage.

Workspace layout and visual specification

At 1440 × 1000, the interface is a dense workspace with a header, left drawing rail, central chart, right watchlist/details column, right navigation rail, and bottom range/time strip. The chart occupies most of the viewport and does not sit inside a conventional scrolling document. The right details area has substantially more content than fits on screen. [E01]

At 390 × 844, the watchlist and right rail are absent, the chart legend becomes more compact, the left tool rail remains, and the range presets become a Date Range menu. Functional inventory

Chart and top toolbar

The top toolbar exposes symbol selection, data-type switching, comparisons, interval, chart style, indicators, indicator templates, alert creation, replay, undo/redo, layout setup, save/manage layouts, quick search, settings, fullscreen, snapshot, community publishing, Trade, and Upgrade. Controls carry accessible labels even when represented by icons. Undo was initially disabled; changing interval, chart style, and symbol produced specific undo labels. Drawing undo/redo was subsequently exercised successfully in the authenticated session. [E01, E08, E09, E18; A08]

The chart legend contains instrument name, resolution, source, market/delay state, OHLC, absolute/percentage change, and Volume. Volume has hide/settings/remove/more controls. Bid/ask-like Sell and Buy boxes also appear on SPX, even though quote metadata marks the index nontradable. A local order action must use instrument capabilities rather than assuming these boxes establish tradability. [E01]

The observed chart-style menu lists:

Family Observed entries
OHLC Bars, Candles, Hollow candles, Volume candles
Lines Line, Line with markers, Step line
Areas Area, HLC area, Baseline
Other conventional Columns, High-low
Order-flow/profile Volume footprint, Time price opportunity, Session volume profile
Transformed/non-time Heikin Ashi, Renko, Line break, Kagi, Point & figure, Range

Entries expose favorite actions and help affordances. Only Candles → Line was exercised. Seeing a menu item does not establish that the anonymous session can use it, that the current instrument supports it, or that its required data is available. Order-flow charts cannot be reconstructed accurately from daily OHLC alone. [E02, E09]

Symbol identity and search

The Symbol search dialog accepts a symbol, ISIN, or CUSIP; supports spread operators; and has All, Stocks, Funds, Futures, Forex, Crypto, Indices, Bonds, Economy, and Options tabs. Results distinguish exchange/provider and instrument type, with expandable groups. Searching SPX returns the SP index, CFDs, a London-listed stock, and unrelated crypto instruments. A ticker string alone is therefore insufficient as a database key. [E02]

Searching NASDAQ:AAPL and pressing Enter selected Apple, changed the chart header and quote/details content, highlighted its watchlist row, and exposed a dividend-adjustment control. The undo label became Undo change symbol. In this scenario the URL still contained symbol=SP%3ASPX. Treat initial deep-link selection and ongoing workspace state as distinct concerns; choose URL synchronization deliberately for the replacement. [E18]

Intervals and visible ranges

The interval menu groups ticks, seconds, minutes, hours, days, and ranges. It includes custom intervals and favorites. Observed entries are:

Group Values

Selecting one hour changed the interval labels and OHLC/volume legend and enabled Undo change resolution. Bar alignment, resampling rules, and numerical equivalence were not exhaustively tested. [E02, E08]

The bottom presets explicitly couple range and resolution: 1D → 1-minute intervals; 5D → 5-minute; 1M → 30-minute; 3M → 1-hour; 6M → 2-hour; YTD and 1Y → daily; 5Y → weekly; All → monthly. This mapping was read from accessible labels, not exercised for every preset. Replicating these as viewport zoom buttons alone would miss part of the specified behavior. Go to and Timezone are separate commands. [E01]

Indicators and scripting

The indicator directory contains personal scripts, purchased scripts, built-in technicals/fundamentals, community/editor selections, trending content, and marketplace navigation. Tabs include Indicators, Strategies, Profiles, Patterns, and Options. Search results mix built-ins and community scripts, with author names and access indicators. Built-in RSI is distinguishable by STD;RSI, not merely its title. [E03, E14]

In the anonymous baseline, selecting that built-in RSI displayed a registration prompt. Authenticated inspection later added its pane, inspected Inputs/Style/Visibility, observed RSI 51.94 and RSI-based MA 55.09, and verified save/reload. Independent formula equivalence remains open. The default Volume series was already present. [E01, E15; A05–A08]

The Pine command opens an editor overlay with an untitled v6 starter indicator, source textbox, save/publish actions, position status, documentation link, and a move-to-split-view command. Authenticated inspection subsequently compiled an authored SMA indicator and mechanics strategy, observed a compiler diagnostic, generated a strategy report, and inspected trades/properties. Remote Pine draft/translation requests were observed. Full language compatibility, named-script persistence, publishing, and debugging remain unverified. [E06; A20–A24]
