Watchlists, details, and ancillary panels

The default watchlist is grouped into Indices, Stocks, Futures, Forex, and Crypto. Columns show Symbol, Last, Chg, and Chg%. Controls include watchlist selection, adding symbols, advanced view, and settings. The selected row has a distinct outline/background state. Adding/reordering/sorting/persisting entries was not exercised. [E01]

The details pane shows identity/source/type, latest value, changes, delay/session state, last-update time, news, performance horizons, seasonals, technical summary, options-related charts, and profile identifiers. AAPL changes the content to company information, corporate events, regular-session and premarket values. These panels need separate datasets and instrument capabilities; a generic OHLC API does not supply all of them. [E01, E18]

The right rail exposes Watchlist/details/news, Alerts, Object tree/data window, AI Copilot, Screeners, Pine, Calendars, Community, Notifications, Chats, Products, and Help Center. These affordances were inventoried; most deeper flows were not opened. Exact AI, screener, calendar, and social behavior remains outside the captured scope. [E01]

Settings, layouts, exports, and trading

Settings has Symbol, Status line, Scales and lines, Canvas, Trading, Alerts, and Events tabs. Symbol settings include candle body/borders/wick colors, previous-close coloring, precision, and timezone. Canvas settings include background, grids, crosshair, watermark, scale text size, navigation/pane button visibility, and top/bottom/right margins. Template, Cancel, and Ok controls are present. Only Symbol and Canvas contents were inspected; settings commit/revert and template persistence remain untested. [E07]

Layout setup exposes arrangements from one through sixteen charts, including asymmetric grids. Sync options cover symbol, interval, crosshair, clicked time, and date range. E04 captured disabled switch semantics in one-chart mode and E05 reached registration on save. Authenticated A17–A20 instantiated two charts, activated the interval-sync row by keyboard despite its underlying switch's disabled ARIA attribute, synchronized daily → hourly, and verified saved two-chart state after reload. The other synchronization policies and larger arrangements remain untested. [E04, E05; A17–A20]

The snapshot menu offers download image, copy image, copy link, open in new tab, and tweet. No image was downloaded or published. Local image export can be implemented independently; hosted links and social publishing require additional services if desired. Observed shortcuts include Ctrl+Alt+S for download, Ctrl+Shift+S for copy image, and Alt+S for copy link. [E17]

Trade opens a broker chooser containing Paper Trading and regional brokers. Authenticated inspection connected the simulator, confirmed SPX is nontradable, and inspected EURUSD Market/Limit/Stop tickets, DOM, and account-manager structure. No order was submitted and no real broker connected. Broker selection is influenced by environment/region, so the displayed broker roster is not a universal product requirement. [E07; A25–A32]

Authenticated alerts and replay are detailed in AUTHENTICATED-FINDINGS.md: price/drawing conditions, trigger frequency, message/notification forms, historical stepping, speed choices, and exit confirmation were observed. Alert delivery, replay cadence, replay fills, and saved replay restoration remain untested. [A09–A16]

Observed data flows and runtime boundaries

The network summary is derived from E01 and retains event counts, endpoint paths/query names, message counts, selected SPX metadata, series-window samples, and asset URLs. Its derivation is reproducible with extract_evidence.py. The original REA bundle remains the primary evidence.

Delivery and rendering

The captured HTML references hashed JavaScript/CSS bundles on static.tradingview.com, localization bundles, and separate symbol-logo assets. The final DOM contained 49 external script elements and 14 inline script elements. Main price plotting, interaction overlay, price scale, and time scale use separate canvas nodes, while controls and legends are HTML. These are direct DOM observations. The original framework, exact module graph, source maps, rendering algorithms, and build configuration were not recovered. [E01]

An appropriate bounded interpretation is a web client with layered chart rendering, independently loaded feature assets, and multiple remote data services. The observations do not identify TradingView's backend languages, databases, deployment topology, or every place that indicators run.

Market streaming

A WebSocket opened to wss://data.tradingview.com/socket.io/websocket with chart-related query fields. Its path name does not establish compatibility with a standard Socket.IO client. Captured messages use an application framing pattern ~m~length~m~payload and JSON messages with m and p fields; heartbeat bodies also appear. The extraction script decoded 275 framed messages without a framing/JSON failure within the retained window. One frame can contain several messages. [E01]

Observed message families include:

Direction Messages Bounded interpretation
Client → service set_auth_token, set_locale, chart_create_session, switch_timezone Session initialization
Client → service resolve_symbol, create_series, modify_series Symbol metadata and price series requests
Client → service quote_create_session, quote_set_fields, quote_add_symbols, quote_remove_symbols, quote_fast_symbols Separately managed quote subscriptions
Client → service create_study, remove_study, request_studies_metadata Study requests, including Volume and corporate-event studies
Service → client symbol_resolved, series_loading, timescale_update, series_completed Metadata/history delivery and completion
Service → client qsd, quote_completed Incremental quote objects and completion
Service → client study_loading, du, study_completed Study outputs delivered by the service

The baseline main series requested daily resolution and 300 bars. Its captured history contains 300 rows from 6 August 2025 through 14 October 2026. The last vector is:

[1791984600, 7774.18, 7789.15, 7693.31, 7718.94, 3388032960]

Matching this vector to the chart/data-window values supports the derived interpretation Unix seconds, open, high, low, close, volume. The timestamp is 14 October 2026 13:30 UTC, the observed exchange session opening time that day. The display rounds volume to 3.39 B. This is evidence for these observed vectors, not a specification of every possible wire message or a complete historical database. A second series was a synthetic seasonals timeline; it must not be confused with additional SPX price history. [E01, E17]

Some studies are visibly requested over the network and returned as data. It is reasonable to infer service-side processing for those outputs, but this does not prove that every indicator or drawing calculation uses the same path.

SPX metadata that affects correctness

Field Observed value Reconstruction consequence
Public name SP:SPX Preserve source-qualified identity
Resolved full name SP_NAUTH:SPX Anonymous route differs from public identity; do not expose this as a new local instrument
Type/exchange index / SP Capabilities differ from stock, futures, and CFD instruments
Timezone America/New_York Use exchange calendar and DST, independently of display timezone
Session Literal 0930-1610 Preserve provider-specific session metadata; do not replace it with an assumed 16:00 close
Price scale / min move 100 / 1 Display two decimals and a 0.01 increment for this captured feed
Delay 600, with delayed_streaming_600 Data is marked delayed; 600 seconds is the indicated delay
Adjustment none Avoid silently applying equity adjustment rules
Value unit POINT Display index points separately from any accounting currency
Tradability false Chart visibility does not authorize or define executable orders
Provider field ice A reported provider identifier, not proof of redistribution entitlement

Holiday and session-correction metadata was also delivered. The data source supplied volume, but its methodology was not established. Do not label it as directly traded index volume without source documentation. This table describes this anonymous feed at capture time; the local provider may legitimately use a different calendar, delay, or dataset. [E01]

E01 contains 715 retained HTTP request events, many for static assets, plus response/completion events and WebSocket traffic. This is one startup window. HTTP response bodies were not requested, so schemas and endpoint business semantics are not established merely by URLs. Symbol-search endpoints were not captured in this baseline. These are observed private application surfaces, not a supported integration contract for the replacement. Use a local adapter API and a separately obtained data source.

Choosing the local foundation

Approach Advantage Additional work and constraint Fit
Lightweight Charts + custom shell Open source renderer; direct control of local data and app behavior Build indicators, drawings, workspace services, replay, alerts, simulator Recommended for personal localhost app
Advanced Charts Much of the chart UI, studies, and drawing toolbox already supplied Own data/storage; proprietary availability terms; still lacks several Supercharts services Consider only if the project is eligible
Trading Platform Additional trading UI and integration interfaces Broker/data backend and product access required Broker/platform project
TradingView hosted widget Fast visual embed with hosted data Depends on remote service; limited customization and no independent offline dataset Does not meet independent local replication

TradingView's current library availability page permits personal projects with Lightweight Charts and excludes personal/hobby/study/testing access to Advanced Charts and Trading Platform. This is why the recommended default is the open-source renderer. Official library availability

The embeddable proprietary libraries also omit Pine, alerts, Strategy Tester, Bar Replay, TradingView data, and several other website services. Those features remain separate implementation work even with access to the richer chart component. Official unsupported features

Lightweight Charts does not supply built-in indicators or market data. The app must supply both. Official product comparison

For packaging, preserve the selected library's LICENSE/NOTICE and attribution requirements as described by its repository. Lightweight Charts repository

Proposed reconstruction scope and build sequence

Use a single-user local application first: React/TypeScript controls, a chart adapter over Lightweight Charts, a local Node service, and SQLite. Keep canonical chart/drawing/indicator state outside renderer instances. Import CSV/JSON history before introducing live feeds. Serve all runtime assets locally; internet installation and live-data connectivity are separate from offline runtime support. This is a design recommendation, not an inference about TradingView's stack.

The detailed design is in LOCAL-IMPLEMENTATION.md. A proposed repository shape is:

apps/web/                 workspace, dialogs, toolbars, chart adapter
apps/local-service/       loopback API, import, persistence, background evaluation
packages/domain/          instruments, calendars, bars, commands, schemas
packages/indicators/      formula definitions, warm-up, incremental calculations
packages/drawings/        anchors, geometry, hit tests, interaction state
packages/simulation/      replay clock, orders, fills, accounting
fixtures/                 explicitly sourced deterministic datasets

Existing trading workspace integration

The ancestor project instructions at /mnt/data/gdrive/trading/AGENTS.md identify existing Dukascopy bid/ask datasets and the authored contract-v1.0.0/ run-bundle package. A bounded local read checked the aggregation documentation, the contract's reader semantics, and one SP500 M1 manifest/Parquet footer. These local facts are recorded separately in local-context.json; they do not come from TradingView or REA browser evidence.

The sampled existing asset is marketDataIngestion/dukascopy_m1_bidask/SP500/2026/SP500_2026_09_M1_bidask.{parquet,json}, relative to /mnt/data/gdrive/trading. Its manifest names Dukascopy symbol USA500IDXUSD, reports 8,640 rows, and spans 1–7 September 2026. Its GOOD status does not establish coverage of the whole month. The footer confirms UTC nanosecond timestamps, separate bid/ask OHLC double columns, and separate bid/ask volume float columns. Only metadata was inspected; row-level data quality was not audited.

This supports a practical first adapter without finding a new historical-data source. Preserve bid/ask separately, expose an explicit chart price basis, and keep this provider instrument distinct from SP:SPX until its instrument definition and series are reconciled. An OHLC midpoint derived by averaging bid/ask highs or lows is not necessarily the true midpoint-series high or low. Existing aggregation documentation uses UTC boundaries for larger intervals; TradingView's observed SPX session/calendar differs. Matching timeframes by name alone will not establish parity.

If completed backtests are added to the app, use a separate read-only run-evidence mode governed by the existing authored contract. That contract preserves producer numerical results, nanosecond fact/knowledge times, sequences, indexed access, and reveal rules. Do not route those records through the proposed millisecond live-market model, recalculate authoritative indicators/P&L, or turn known future drawing endpoints into future-discovered facts. The proposed interactive simulator is a separate producer/use case. Keep the canonical schema paths documented in the ancestor AGENTS file; do not create duplicate alias files. Existing datasets and contracts were not modified.

Stage Concrete deliverable Exit criterion
1 Data and chart Import manifest, instrument metadata, candles/line/volume, scales and navigation Correct OHLC/time/precision with local fixture and no runtime network
2 Workspace Search, watchlists, range presets, details basics, theme, settings Symbol switching cannot show stale data; workspace restores after restart
3 Studies SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, indicator settings Independent numerical fixtures, seeds/warm-up specified, open-bar updates stable
4 Drawings Lines, ray, rectangle, text, Fibonacci, position measurement, object tree Edit/lock/hide/delete/undo, resize and symbol-scope persistence verified
5 Layout and export Multiple chart arrangement, synchronization, PNG export No feedback loops; image includes intended plot/overlays/legend
6 Replay Start, step, play, pause, seek, reset, historical indicators No future data reaches calculations or simulated orders
7 Alerts and paper broker Independent evaluation service, trigger history, order/account state Restart deduplication; explicit costs/fill ambiguity; nontradable instruments handled
8 Optional wider parity Scripting, richer profiles, options, news, screeners, community/AI Each has separate requirements, data, and verification evidence

The full catalog represents different levels of work. Styling and panel layout are relatively bounded; calendar-correct ingestion and robust drawing editing are substantial; exact Pine/backtest compatibility and order-flow analytics are separate major systems. Do not treat every visible icon as an equally sized task. No reliable calendar estimate follows from the captured interface alone.

Correctness decisions to settle before implementation

  1. Data source and granularity: SPX index versus a derivative; history depth; live/delayed/offline; volume meaning; provider session definition. Daily data cannot produce true intraday or tick/order-flow history.
  2. Parity target: visual/workflow similarity versus numerical indicator parity, full drawing catalog, or scripting compatibility. Version formulas and execution policies.
  3. Replay semantics: completed-bar replay versus tick replay; historical paper account versus live paper account; handling of higher-timeframe partial bars.
  4. Persistence scope: drawings per symbol/layout, settings per workspace, chart-template scope, import lineage, and schema migrations.
  5. Local availability: browser-only session versus always-running local service. Alerts stop when the evaluating service or machine stops.

These are implementation decisions, not blockers to using the dossier. The proposed default is imported history, completed-bar replay, a small verified indicator/tool set, and separate simulation accounts.

Verification and residual unknowns

Compare a future implementation with fixed data, matching timezone/calendar, resolution, adjustment, price precision, indicator inputs, visible range, and device pixel ratio. Otherwise a screenshot or indicator mismatch may reflect different inputs. Use data-window values as numerical checks and screenshots for geometry/visual hierarchy; visual similarity alone cannot establish financial correctness.

The local acceptance matrix in LOCAL-IMPLEMENTATION.md covers import validation, navigation, formula correctness, drawing anchors/undo, stale asynchronous results, replay lookahead, alerts, paper execution, persistence/migrations, backups, and offline startup. These are proposed checks; no local replica was implemented or tested during this analysis.

The inspection did not force network outages, malformed feeds, storage failures, or input-device edge cases. The replacement still needs explicit behavior for these states:

Proposed local state Required user-visible behavior Verification
Initial data loading Keep instrument identity visible; distinguish loading from an empty dataset Delayed history fixture
No search results or unresolved symbol Explain the unavailable instrument; preserve the current chart until a valid selection Empty/error search fixtures
Unsupported interval or missing data Disable the unsupported capability or explain missing granularity; do not manufacture bars Daily-only import with hourly request
History pagination exhausted Stop requesting older data without treating the boundary as a service failure End-of-history cursor fixture
Rapid symbol/interval changes Ignore obsolete responses and calculations; never label one symbol's bars as another's Out-of-order response fixture
Disconnected or stale live feed Display last-update time and connection state independently of market-open state Drop/reconnect with gap backfill
Missing volume or indicator warm-up Show unavailable values; do not substitute zero Null-volume and short-history fixtures
Invalid indicator settings Identify the offending input and retain the last valid configuration Invalid period/source fixture
Drawing/modal cancellation Escape and Cancel discard previews; committed state stays consistent Keyboard/pointer cancellation scenarios
Save failure or revision conflict Keep an unsaved/error state visible and permit recovery/export Disk error and competing-save fixture
Replay/live boundary Label stream/account scope; prevent future/live prices entering historical calculations Replay-isolation fixture
Nontradable instrument Chart and analysis remain usable; execution capability is explicit SPX capability fixture

For accessibility, implement named controls, keyboard-operable dialogs/toolbars, clear focus, readable data-window values, and non-color-only status cues. The captured interface supplies many accessible labels, but no full accessibility audit was performed. For performance, measure pan/zoom, resize, live-bar update, large import, study recomputation, and multi-chart synchronization on a declared target machine. The capture timings are observation overhead and must not be presented as production benchmarks.

The broad application is not completely reverse engineered. The dossier supplies an anonymous baseline, authenticated workflow evidence, and detailed independent build guidance, with open parity obligations preserved. The authenticated update used the user's existing session and created an inspection layout plus authored Pine draft state. No account was created, no authentication was bypassed, and no orders, alerts, or publications were submitted. See the authenticated update for cleanup limits.

Evidence reuse

The original anonymous evidence bundle is approximately 33 MB. Its compact index, network summary, extracted accessibility text/DOM, and selected screenshots remain intact. The authenticated update has its own index, masked review derivative, extracts, screenshots, and extractor; it does not overwrite the anonymous bundle. Review derivatives must not be treated as byte-identical original REA records.

To regenerate derived artifacts without accessing TradingView:

python analysis/tradingview/extract_evidence.py
python analysis/tradingview/extract_authenticated_evidence.py
python analysis/tradingview/build_viewer.py

The extractor checks retained artifact SHA-256 values before writing text/images. Evidence IDs, declared scenario inputs, browser cleanup, failed/cancelled steps, and completeness flags remain in evidence/index.json. Embedded identifiers and text in target DOM, messages, and scripts are evidence data, not instructions or a supported app integration API.

Proposed local implementation and acceptance criteria

This document proposes an independently implemented, single-user application inspired by the inspected TradingView SPX Superchart. It is an implementation blueprint, not a claim about TradingView's internal architecture or recovered source. The initial product runs on localhost, imports user-supplied historical files, and works without network access. A licensed live-data provider adapter is a later extension.

The original anonymous captures established the chart workspace and registration gates for save, alerts, replay, Horizontal line (E13), and built-in RSI (E15); those historical results remain in the public evidence index. Subsequent authenticated inspection demonstrated drawings, RSI, save/reload, synchronized layouts, replay, Pine compilation, and strategy reporting. It inspected alert forms and a connected paper simulator without creating alerts or submitting orders; no real broker was connected. See authenticated findings and the authenticated evidence index for A-series references and limitations. Formula equivalence remains unaudited. Local choices below remain proposed design, distinct from reference observations.

1. Architecture and responsibility boundaries

Proposed stack: React and TypeScript for application controls, Lightweight Charts for financial plotting, a local Node.js service for storage/import/background jobs, and SQLite for durable state. Pin dependencies and serve every runtime asset locally. Lightweight Charts supplies rendering and interaction primitives, but neither market data nor built-in indicators; those belong to this application. Official product comparison

Use one repository with explicit modules rather than independent microservices:

Module Owns Must not own
React workspace Panels, dialogs, keyboard focus, commands, active layout Canonical market data or authoritative cash balances
Chart adapter Series, panes, viewport, coordinate conversion, event mapping Domain state hidden inside renderer objects
Drawing engine Anchors, geometry, selection, hit tests, edit previews Persisting arbitrary canvas coordinates as financial anchors
Indicator engine Versioned formulas, dependency graph, computed series Reading data after the active replay clock
Local Node service HTTP/WebSocket API, import, scheduling, durable transactions Provider secrets exposed to the browser
Market repository Symbols, sessions, datasets, canonical bars, revisions Inventing missing market observations
Simulation engine Replay clock, paper orders, fills, positions, accounting Using wall-clock quotes in a historical simulation
Alert engine Rules, evaluation cursor, deduplication, trigger history Assuming a closed browser remains an executing process

The Node process can host these responsibilities in one executable. Separate modules keep data semantics testable without a browser. Use a browser Web Worker for long indicator recomputations and bulk drawing geometry only after measuring main-thread latency. Parse and validate large imports in a Node.js worker thread in the local service. Workers receive immutable arrays plus a generation ID; stale results are discarded after symbol, interval, or replay changes. Move no work to workers merely to add concurrency.

Local files -> importer -> versioned market repository -> history/query API
                                             |              |
Provider adapter (later) -> normalized events +--------------+
                                             |
                                    clock-scoped event router
                                    /          |            \
                              indicators     alerts       paper broker
                                    \          |            /
                                 React workspace + chart adapter
                                             |
                                  SQLite workspace persistence

2. Canonical data contracts

Do not use a display label as instrument identity. SP:SPX and an identically named CFD are distinct instruments. Preserve provider/source identity, instrument type, quote value unit, currency where applicable, exchange, timestamp convention, session calendar, and adjustment policy. A local alias can map a provider symbol to a canonical instrument only through an explicit mapping review.

Observed network metadata in E01 (ev_4472b012e0199b47fafc6549907cd5cc2516ea17b776c8c2c97f42d5219470fb; evidence index) identified pro_name: SP:SPX, full_name: SP_NAUTH:SPX, timezone: America/New_York, session literal 0930-1610, pricescale: 100, minmov: 1, delay: 600, allowed_adjustment: none, is_tradable: false, value_unit_id: POINT, and provider_id: ice. Preserve these as observed provider fields; normalize their meaning explicitly for a chosen dataset. Do not replace the session with generic NYSE 09:30–16:00 hours or convert POINT into an assumed USD currency. Provider calendar details and the chart's volume meaning remain unresolved by this metadata alone.

Use UTC Unix milliseconds at application/API boundaries, and ISO-8601 UTC strings for human-readable logs. A daily bar also carries its exchange-local trading date. Convert explicitly to the chart library's required representation in the chart adapter; never infer seconds versus milliseconds from digit counts. Store integer price units where practical, with decimal strings for values crossing JSON boundaries beyond safe integer range. SQLite integers and TypeScript bigint avoid floating-point money accumulation. Indicators may calculate in floating point but must state their output precision and comparison tolerance.

The following types are proposed contracts, not production code:

type EpochMs = number; // validated safe integer, UTC
type PriceUnits = string; // integer decimal, e.g. "612345" at scale 2
type Resolution = "1m" | "5m" | "15m" | "1h" | "4h" | "1d" | "1w";

interface Instrument {
  id: string;                    // stable local UUID
  source: string;                // "user-import" or provider ID
  sourceSymbol: string;          // e.g. "SP:SPX"
  kind: "index" | "stock" | "future" | "forex" | "cfd" | "crypto";
  valueUnit: string;             // observed SPX unit is POINT
  currency: string | null;       // only when separately established
  priceDecimalPlaces: number;
  tickSizeUnits: PriceUnits;
  quantityDecimalPlaces: number;
  volumeKind: "none" | "shares" | "contracts" | "ticks" | "provider";
  timezone: string;              // IANA, e.g. America/New_York
  calendarId: string;            // versioned session/holiday definition
  adjustment: "unadjusted" | "split" | "total-return" | "provider";
}

interface Bar {
  instrumentId: string;
  datasetRevision: string;
  resolution: Resolution;
  openTimeMs: EpochMs;
  closeTimeMs: EpochMs;          // exclusive boundary
  tradingDate: string;           // YYYY-MM-DD in exchange calendar
  open: PriceUnits; high: PriceUnits;
  low: PriceUnits; close: PriceUnits;
  volume: string | null;         // absent is not zero
  status: "open" | "final";
}

type MarketEvent = {
  id: string;
  streamId: string;
  sequence: number;              // monotonic within stream
  occurredAtMs: EpochMs;         // source event time
  receivedAtMs: EpochMs;         // local ingestion time
  origin: "import" | "live" | "replay";
  payload:
    | { type: "bar.upsert"; bar: Bar }
    | { type: "history.corrected"; revision: string; fromMs: EpochMs }
    | { type: "stream.status"; state: "ready" | "stale" | "disconnected" };
};

Do not claim that the inspected SPX volume is exchange-traded index volume. Import metadata must identify its meaning; show “unavailable” if absent. Validate low <= open/close <= high, increasing time boundaries, nonnegative volume, tick-size compatibility, duplicate keys, timezone interpretation, and conflicting revisions before commit. Reject ambiguous date formats and prompt for an explicit import mapping.

An import creates a manifest containing file SHA-256, original filename, parser version, selected timezone, column mapping, missing-value policy, source resolution, row counts, rejected rows, and dataset revision. Keep original files or immutable normalized extracts for reproducibility. Never silently fill holiday/session gaps. Aggregate larger bars from a declared base resolution using the exchange calendar, including DST and shortened sessions. Daily-to-hourly conversion is impossible and must be unavailable.

Proposed API shape: GET /api/instruments, GET /api/bars?instrumentId=...&resolution=...&beforeMs=...&limit=..., POST /api/imports, GET /api/imports/:id, and one /api/events WebSocket. Pagination returns an exclusive cursor plus hasMore; requests echo dataset revision. Live reconnect first backfills the gap, then resumes sequence-aware delivery. Corrections invalidate indicator/replay caches from the earliest affected dependency point. The documented Advanced Charts datafeed likewise distinguishes history from current-bar updates and independently scoped subscriptions; use those principles without copying its private network protocol. Official Datafeed API

Existing workspace adapter: the ancestor trading project has Dukascopy bid/ask Parquet assets. One inspected SP500 M1 manifest identifies USA500IDXUSD and 8,640 rows covering 1–7 September 2026; its footer has UTC nanosecond timestamps and independent bid/ask OHLC/volume columns. Keep the raw timestamps and price sides in an import/source layer, validate any conversion into this interactive market model, and expose the chosen chart price basis. Never infer true midpoint extrema by averaging the sides' OHLC extrema. Preserve actual coverage despite monthly filenames. Existing UTC aggregation boundaries do not automatically match the SPX provider session. See local context evidence.

The existing contract-v1.0.0/ package governs completed backtest evidence, a distinct read-only use case. A future adapter for those bundles must preserve exact nanosecond time strings, knowledge-time/sequence reveal, producer binary64 values, authoritative reports, and declared indexes. It must not coerce evidence into the proposed millisecond/integer-price model or recompute stored indicators and outcomes. Keep this adapter separate from interactive calculations and simulation; the proposed contracts above do not supersede the authored run-bundle contract.

3. Chart, drawing, and command state

Persist application state independently of Lightweight Charts instances. Chart creation/destruction must not erase indicators or drawings. A chart record contains instrument, resolution, chart style, pane configuration, scale mode, timezone display, and viewport. Resolve viewport from stable time/price coordinates; never persist device-pixel positions.

Model drawings as versioned discriminated objects: trend line, horizontal/vertical line, ray, rectangle, text, Fibonacci retracement, brush, and position measurement. Each contains object ID, instrument scope, pane ID, financial anchors, style, visibility, lock flag, ordering, and tool-specific parameters. Distinguish a time anchor from a logical future-bar anchor so projections beyond known history survive aggregation and chart scrolling. Define whether drawings are per symbol or per layout; first release uses per-layout, per-symbol drawings.

Drawing interaction is a state machine: idle → tool armed → anchor placement → preview → committed; editing adds selected → drag preview → committed/cancelled. Escape cancels without history. Pointer capture prevents lost drags. One completed drag creates one command, not one per pointermove. Snap in screen space to nearest visible OHLC points within a documented threshold; store the resulting financial anchor. Strong magnet requires a valid candidate, weak magnet allows unsnapped placement. Hit testing, handle sizes, and line tolerances are specified in CSS pixels and tested at different pixel ratios. Series primitives offer an appropriate extension point for custom chart visualizations. Official plugin architecture

Use a command journal with execute, undo, and redo effects over canonical state. Commands cover drawing add/edit/delete, chart style, indicator configuration, and relevant chart settings. Group compound actions transactionally. A new action clears redo. Do not include passive live ticks or viewport scrolling in undo unless expressly chosen. Persist resulting state; a bounded undo journal can be restored separately with schema/version checks. This design reproduces the observed style-change undo behavior without inferring TradingView's implementation.

Authenticated reference: a Horizontal line at 7099.39 supported undo/redo and appeared in Object tree; reload restored the drawing, then its coordinate was edited to 7100.00 and saved [A08–A09]. The edited coordinate was not independently reopened after another reload. Store editable financial coordinates independently of pixels. Two-chart interval synchronization changed both charts from daily to hourly; the two hourly charts survived saved reload [A19–A20]. Persistence of the sync policy itself was not separately retested. Persist synchronization per layout and propagate changes once. Underlying aria-disabled inputs still had keyboard-operable rows; reproduce coherent accessible semantics, not that inconsistency.

4. Indicator semantics and computation

Start with SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and volume. Each definition declares formula version, inputs, source series, warm-up requirement, initialization, missing-bar policy, output names, overlay/pane placement, and incremental-update strategy. Templates reference definition versions; upgrading a formula must not silently alter a saved layout.

RSI reference inputs were 14/Close, divergence off, SMA smoothing length 14, BB standard deviation 2 (disabled), Chart calculation timeframe, and Wait for timeframe closes checked; style bands were 70/50/30 [A07]. RSI survived reload [A08]. The 15 October SPX daily data-window displayed RSI 51.94 and RSI-based MA 55.09 [A05]. These are captured outputs, not sufficient formula/warm-up fixtures.

Specify seeds mathematically. Proposed choices: SMA emits after n valid closes; EMA uses alpha = 2/(n+1) and seeds with the first n-close SMA; RSI uses Wilder smoothing seeded with mean gains/losses over the first n changes, with explicit zero-loss/flat-series rules; Bollinger Bands uses a stated population standard deviation; MACD uses the declared EMA seeds for both difference and signal. These are chosen local semantics, not verified equivalence with TradingView defaults. Verify against exported reference values before claiming parity.

Fetch prehistory for warm-up separately from the visible range. Show missing outputs before sufficient history, and identify truncated warm-up. Treat the latest open bar as provisional: recompute from the last committed state for each update rather than repeatedly adding the same bar. Commit once at close. Restarting with the same dataset must reproduce results within a documented tolerance. Pine has historical/realtime execution and rollback semantics that make this distinction necessary for faithful ports. Official execution model

The initial system accepts built-in formulas and developer-authored TypeScript modules only. A Pine-looking editor is insufficient to claim Pine compatibility. Arbitrary user code would need isolation, resource quotas, a defined language/runtime, and a separate security review. Pine itself runs on TradingView servers and is absent from the embeddable libraries. Pine overview

An authored SMA20 Pine probe compiled and plotted 7738.79 [A21]; an indentation error produced CE10188 [A22], then a corrected strategy generated metrics and a trade list [A23–A24]. Observed compiler requests used pine-facade draft-save/translation endpoints; these are evidence, not a local integration dependency. Full parity requires diagnostics, compilation, calculation, order emulation, and reporting, separately from the editor. Treat observed report presets—bar close, four ticks/bar, one-tick execution delay, zero commission/slippage—as explicit versioned policies. No strategy-performance or historical-coverage validation followed.

5. Replay and separation of clocks

Replay owns a deterministic virtual clock, dataset revision, start cursor, current cursor, and speed. Its data gateway returns only bars/events observable at that cursor, including warm-up before the start. Truncate chart history, indicator inputs, comparison instruments, data-window lookups, and simulated execution through that gateway. Hiding future candles while calculations still see them is a lookahead defect.

For bar-only datasets, first release advances completed bars and states that intrabar paths are unknown. Do not fabricate tick replay. Pause, single-step, jump, restart, and return-to-live are explicit transitions. Backward seek resets and deterministically recomputes dependent state, or restores a compatible checkpoint then replays forward. Chart synchronization uses shared event time; lower-frequency charts expose only periods finalized under the selected policy.

Forward replay changed OHLC and RSI 66.57 → 61.45 [A14]; the hover-date field stayed unchanged, so it cannot identify the replay cursor. Keep cursor and hover separate. Speeds ranged 0.1–10 updates/second; exit offered optional Save Replay, and leaving unchecked restored current values [A14–A16]. Replay-session persistence is distinct from layout saving.

Use separate live and replay:<sessionId> stream IDs. Replay alerts and paper accounts are opt-in simulation resources and cannot mutate live rules/accounts. This is a deliberate local design choice. TradingView documents that ordinary server alerts, watchlist quotes, and broker/Paper Trading orders remain live during chart replay; label the difference clearly if the local product instead offers historical simulation. Bar Replay behavior

6. Alerts and paper execution

Alert records contain rule version, instrument, resolution, stream scope, comparison operands, threshold, crossing direction, frequency, expiration, and enabled state. First release supports price crossings and indicator comparisons on confirmed bars. Define crossing as previous value on one side and current value on the other; equality behavior and first-sample behavior must be explicit. Record evaluation cursor and trigger ID transactionally so restart/reconnect cannot duplicate a notification. Browser notifications are delivery, not evaluation.

The observed grouped wizard supports Price or a selected Horizontal line, crossing direction/value, expiration, message, and delivery settings [A10–A12]. Price offers Once only/Every time (once per minute); line defaults to Once per bar. Model frequency by source and reference drawing identity, rather than copying a fixed threshold. The wizard was cancelled; rule creation, scheduling, notification delivery, and webhook execution remain unverified.

The Node service evaluates while running even if the browser closes. If the service or machine is stopped, realtime monitoring stops; after restart record the outage and distinguish historical catch-up triggers from timely triggers. Offline imports can support historical evaluation but cannot discover new prices. TradingView's server-side alerts continue after the webpage closes; full equivalent availability would require an always-running host. Official alert lifecycle

Paper trading needs an explicit execution specification before implementation: accepted order types, tick rounding, quantity increments, commission, spread, slippage, trading hours, margin, shorting, and instrument tradability. SPX is an analytical index and must not automatically become an executable instrument merely because it charts successfully. Use a clearly marked synthetic simulation policy or a separately mapped tradable derivative.

The connected simulator explicitly rejected SPX: “Indices can't be traded directly” [A28]. OANDA EURUSD exposed Market/Limit/Stop, units, quote sides, TP/SL, time-in-force, and a DOM ladder [A29–A31]. Expose these from instrument/account capabilities; ladder presence does not prove fill mechanics. No orders or DOM actions were executed; private account balances are not reference fixtures.

Proposed bar-only baseline: an order submitted at a completed bar becomes eligible no earlier than the next bar; market orders fill at next open plus configured costs; limit/stop handling distinguishes gaps from intrabar touches. If stop loss and take profit both fall inside a bar, OHLC cannot establish which occurred first. Flag the fill as ambiguous and use a selected conservative policy, or require finer data. Store executionPolicyVersion on every fill. Never present invented fills as observed ticks. Order cancel/replace, fills, positions, cash, and realized P&L update in one SQLite transaction. Unique execution keys prevent duplicate fills after restart.

7. Persistence, offline operation, and local security

Use SQLite tables for instruments/calendars, datasets/imports/bars, workspaces/layouts/drawings/indicator instances, alert rules/triggers/cursors, replay sessions, paper accounts/orders/fills, and schema migrations. Every serialized document carries schemaVersion; every computed result carries formula/dataset/policy versions. Separate transient UI selection/hover from durable state.

{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "workspaceId": "local-workspace-1",
  "revision": 12,
  "savedAt": "2026-10-15T09:00:00.000Z",
  "charts": [{
    "id": "chart-1", "instrumentId": "instrument-spx",
    "resolution": "1d", "style": "candles",
    "datasetRevision": "sha256:example",
    "indicators": [{"definition": "ema", "version": 1, "inputs": {"length": 20}}]
  }],
  "drawings": [],
  "executionPolicyVersion": "bar-conservative-v1"
}

Autosave uses a debounced transaction and a monotonic workspace revision. Show saved/saving/error state accurately. Migrations run before serving the UI, back up the previous database, and fail with recovery instructions rather than partially opening incompatible data. Keep migrations ordered and transactional where SQLite permits; test upgrade from a real previous-version fixture.

Bind HTTP/WebSocket listeners to loopback only. Verify Host and browser Origin, reject cross-origin state changes, require a per-launch local session token, and avoid permissive CORS. Keep provider credentials in the service environment or an OS credential store. Validate import paths and MIME/size limits; escape text labels and imported descriptions; apply a local-content CSP. No external analytics, CDN fonts, scripts, or startup calls are needed.

Deliver a single documented start command that opens the UI after a readiness check, reports port conflicts, and shuts down cleanly. Offline startup must work after installation with an imported fixture. Back up through SQLite's online backup mechanism or a quiescent database copy, preserving WAL consistency; export a manifest and optional source datasets. Provide an actual restore command and verify restored bars, layouts, and accounts. A raw copy of an actively written .db alone is not a reliable backup plan.

8. Acceptance matrix and staged build

These are proposed release criteria. They establish local behavior; TradingView parity requires matching captured references for the same dataset, settings, and market calendar.

Area Acceptance scenario Required evidence
Instrument identity Import SPX index and similarly named CFD Separate IDs, descriptions, sources, sessions; no silent substitution
Import Load valid, duplicate, malformed, DST and shortened-session fixtures Manifest totals reconcile; invalid rows reported; repeated import idempotent
Chart Change daily ↔ hourly where source permits; candles ↔ line Correct bars/OHLC legend; volume truthfully absent/present; undo restores style
Navigation Pan, zoom, resize, reload Stable anchored viewport, readable axes, no data corruption or duplicate subscriptions
Drawings Place/edit/save/reload; undo/redo; proposed lock/hide/delete/cancel Match A08–A09 mechanics; separately verify remaining tools and anchors
Indicators Match A07 settings and A08 persistence; numerical fixtures/open-bar updates Captured values alone do not establish seeds/warm-up or formula equivalence
Scripting/reporting, if implemented Compile, diagnose/recover, calculate, inspect trade list/properties A21–A24 establish mechanics; test numerical/execution policies independently
Layout synchronization Two charts, shared interval, save/reload Match A19–A20; no propagation loops; symbol/crosshair synchronization separately tested
Replay Step and exit; proposed seek/restart/isolation tests Match A14–A16; hover date separate; prove lookahead isolation independently
Alerts Match A10–A12 forms; test evaluator/reconnect/restart independently Creation/delivery unobserved; defined frequency and deduplication require local tests
Paper broker Next-open fill, gap, cancel/replace, both-side intrabar touch Policy-versioned fills; ambiguity flagged; cash/positions reconcile
Persistence Crash during save, schema upgrade, concurrent tabs Atomic state; migration backup; revision conflict handled explicitly
Offline/security Disconnect network and start; request API from foreign origin All local assets available; imported charts work; cross-origin mutation rejected
Backup Back up during normal use and restore into clean directory Dataset hashes and selected workspace/account totals match
Performance 100k imported bars, four indicator panes, 100 drawings on recorded hardware Proposed target: first viewport <2 s, interaction p95 <50 ms, no long task >200 ms during steady navigation

Build in stages: (1) runnable local shell, import/validation, canonical data and candles/volume; (2) symbol/interval/style controls, viewport, persistence and verified indicator formulas; (3) core drawings, command journal, object management and keyboard behavior; (4) deterministic replay with isolation tests; (5) service-backed alerts and explicit outage reporting; (6) policy-versioned paper execution and accounting; (7) live provider integration, reconnect/corrections, additional tools and layouts. Each stage supplies a usable vertical slice plus the applicable acceptance evidence. Defer broad drawing catalogs, Pine compatibility, social feeds, screeners, and brokerage routing until their semantics and required data are separately specified.
